Not sure how I feel about this article. On the one had, if you take what Valve is saying at face-value, you'd be led to think that they're being altruistic. On the other hand, this is business and money is involved so you have to look at the economics of it. Effectively what Valve is doing is loaning money to developers that is predicated on being paid back from future earnings of their title being published on Steam. So in other words, they're not as much paying for developers to do non-exclusivity as they are loaning money against the requirement to publish on Steam as well.

I can't say I blame them because they're in a tight spot what with MS and Sony both having deep pockets to pay for exclusives whereas Valve can't play that game as effectively. This scheme seems to be somewhat viable, but is unlikely to persuade big developers producing AAA titles. It's about as good a strategy as they can probably come up with, but it certainly isn't altrustic...it's 100% in their business interest.

That's a good point. Whenever a company makes a seemingly-altruistic business decision, it's usually just a case of consumer interest and corporate interests aligning. I don't think corporations have a "conscience", but I'll support whenever their interests align with consumers' interests in the hopes that they'll continue to consider consumers in their business decisions.
